verify.note: The owner's play recorded in Fuse (heart_h1.rzx, `rzx strip` of its autosaves) and six scripted recordings, all from the archive snapshot at the tape's BASIC start. Each hook against the original from one state: every register with R, all game memory, the sprites against a model of the noted figures and against the game's own picture.

status.title: Heartland
status.build: heartland_sprites.nex 7a14d2f1 (every figure a sprite in bright white laid on its own pixels; the game's memory and the screen bitmap stay the original's; only the white paint under large figures is kept off the screen; whole alt ROM image, the snapshot's own BASIC start; pace limiter)
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on 7 recordings, 25,639 frames (R compared): the owner's play in Fuse (heart_h1, 12,178 frames) and 6 scripted; unit PASS (119 cases, the game's interrupt inside every hook among them); 11 broken builds, 11 detected; ROM path check pass; hooks' time +0.32% of the recordings' time over the copies they stand for
status.next: hardware test; Enhanced colours and colour sheets (patterns made ahead)

techniques.target: the random routine (0xBBF3) reads a byte at address A * 257 anywhere in memory: buffer and bitmap stay the original's; the two attribute cells it can read with the paint lifted (0x5959, 0x5A5A) are answered with the original's colour
the game's plotters and screen copy unchanged; each sprite lies on its figure's own pixels in the bitmap, switched in one attribute run after the copy
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set / hlib_r_add at every hook; the two wrapped copies get the original's R at their call, the attribute copy a correction of 2 per cell under the ink limit
HLIB_SPEED_IN / OUT in every hook but the random byte's (it stays at the game's speed); the attribute copy runs the game's routine at the latched speed
one window around the screen copy (targets 4667 / 5998 sixteenths of a line for 112 / 144 lines); notes, paints and the attribute copy pay into the debt
both builds: Sinclair's ROM as alt image 1, so the snapshot's BASIC (PAUSE 0, RANDOMIZE USR 25000) runs as on a 48K; the stubs end below 0x3939

results.scope: 7 recordings, 25,639 frames, 267 random bytes (38 read from the screen, 0 where the paint is lifted); the random byte at all 256 addresses and from a cell with its paint lifted in unit cases; no hardware

5,026 screen copies: 3,158,110 sprite pixels equal to a model of the noted figures and on the same pixels of the game's buffer, but 275 bolt pixels the original XORs into a figure; software model only, no frame capture, no hardware

the game's interrupt taken at 13 points inside each of the 7 hooks from one captured state each: the same memory, registers and sprites as the interrupt after the hook; pace on the simulator's line clock only

pacing.coverage: Seven recordings (one human), 25,639 frames; the screen copy's own time read off the verifier's run of the routine (65,335 T for 112 lines, 83,978 T for 144); hook time on the simulator's line clock. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: The copy hook runs the game's copy at 28 MHz and waits out the rest of its time; the other hooks pay into the debt. Hooks' time +0.32% of the recordings' time over the copies they stand for.

dependencies.coverage: Every reader and writer of the back buffer in the owner's first 5,000 frames (scan --writers); the interrupt handler's memory use over all recordings (isr); the three plotters, the paint, both copies, the random routine.
dependencies.result: The random routine reads any byte of memory, so the buffer, the saved bytes and the bitmap stay the original's; the attribute file differs in the painted cells, of which the routine can read two, answered with the original's colour.

feasibility.decision: Sprites laid over the figures the game still draws (owner's defaults of 2026-11-17: bright white figures, rooms on the ULA, figures behind the foreground pieces); the first design, figures out of the buffer, failed the whole-state comparison and was dropped.
feasibility.next_experiment: Hardware: the checklist in games/heartland.md; pace against the original over a minute of walking (update-keyed): within 2%.
